title.zh: 卷一百八十 列傳第六十七: 耶律希亮 趙世延 孔思晦
title.en: Volume 180 Biographies 67: Yelu Xiliang, Zhao Shiyan, Kong Sihui
title.raw: 卷一百八十 列傳第六十七: 耶律希亮 趙世延 孔思晦 Volume 180 Biographies 67: Yelu Xiliang, Zhao Shiyan, Kong Sihui

sentences.zh: 耶律希亮

translations.literal: Yelü Xiliang
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Xiliang

sentences.zh: 耶律希亮，字明甫，楚材之孫，鑄之子也。

translations.literal: Yelü Xiliang, courtesy name Mingfu, was the grandson of Chucai and the son of Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Xiliang, whose courtesy name was Mingfu, was a grandson of Yelü Chucai and a son of Yelü Zhu.

sentences.zh: 初，六皇后命以赤帖吉氏歸鑄，生希亮於和林南之涼樓，曰禿忽思，六皇后遂以其地名之。

translations.literal: At first, Empress Dowager Töregene ordered that Chijiteji be given to Zhu in marriage; Xiliang was born at the Cool Tower south of Karakorum, called Tuhusi, and the empress dowager then named him after that place.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Dowager Töregene had given Chijiteji in marriage to Zhu. Xiliang was born at the Cool Tower south of Karakorum, a place called Tuhusi, and the empress dowager named him after it.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘗遣鑄核錢糧於燕，鑄曰：「臣先世皆讀儒書，儒生俱在中土，願攜諸子，至燕受業。

translations.literal: Emperor Möngke once sent Zhu to audit money and grain in Yan; Zhu said, "My forebears for generations all read Confucian books, and Confucian scholars are all in the Central Plains; I wish to take my sons to Yan to receive instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Möngke once dispatched Zhu to Yan to audit revenue and supplies. Zhu said, "For generations my family has studied the Confucian classics, and the scholars are all in China proper. I ask permission to bring my sons to Yan for their education."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗從之，乃命希亮師事北平趙衍。

translations.literal: Emperor Möngke assented and thereupon ordered Xiliang to take Zhao Yan of Beiping as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed Xiliang to study under Zhao Yan of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 時方九歲，未浹旬，已能賦詩。

translations.literal: He was then nine years old; before ten days had passed, he could already compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was only nine years old, yet within ten days he was already writing verse.

sentences.zh: 歲丙辰，憲宗召鑄還和林，希亮獨留燕。

translations.literal: In the year bingchen, Emperor Möngke summoned Zhu back to Karakorum, and Xiliang alone remained in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year, Emperor Möngke recalled Zhu to Karakorum while Xiliang stayed behind in Yan.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，憲宗在六盤山，希亮詣行在所。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu, Emperor Möngke was at Liupanshan; Xiliang went to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year the emperor was at Liupanshan, and Xiliang went to join the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 已而鑄扈從南伐，希亮亦在行。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu followed in attendance on the southern campaign, and Xiliang was also on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhu accompanied the southern expedition, and Xiliang marched with him.

sentences.zh: 明年，憲宗崩於蜀，希亮將輜重北歸陝右。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Möngke died in Shu; Xiliang escorted the baggage train north back to the Shaanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Möngke died in Shu, and Xiliang led the supply train northward back into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 又明年，為中統元年，世祖即位，阿里不哥反，遣使召主將渾都海。

translations.literal: The year after that was the first year of Zhongtong; Emperor Kublai ascended the throne, Ariq Böke rebelled, and sent envoys to summon the commander Hunduhai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year was the first year of Zhongtong. Kublai took the throne, Ariq Böke rose in revolt, and sent envoys to summon the commander Hunduhai.

sentences.zh: 鑄說渾都海等入朝，皆不從，則棄其妻子，挺身來歸。

translations.literal: Zhu urged Hunduhai and the others to come to court; none obeyed, so he abandoned wife and children and came alone to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu urged Hunduhai and the others to present themselves at court, but they refused. He then left his wife and children behind and came alone to join Kublai.

sentences.zh: 既而渾都海知鑄去，怒，遣百騎追之不及。

translations.literal: Before long Hunduhai learned that Zhu had gone, was enraged, and sent a hundred horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunduhai learned that Zhu had fled, he flew into a rage and sent a hundred horsemen in pursuit, but they could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 乃使百人監視希亮母子，迫脅使從行，自靈武過應吉里城，至西涼甘州。

translations.literal: He then sent a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in Xiliang.
translations.idiomatic: He then set a hundred men to guard Xiliang and his mother and forced them to march with the army from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in Xiliang.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥遣大將阿藍答兒自和林帥師至焉支山，希亮見之。

translations.literal: Ariq Böke dispatched the great general Alandar from Karakorum leading troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Böke sent the general Alandar from Karakorum at the head of an army to Yanzhi Mountain, where Xiliang was brought before him.

sentences.zh: 阿藍答兒問：「而父安在？

translations.literal: Alandar asked, "Where is your father?"
translations.idiomatic: Alandar asked, "Where is your father?"

sentences.zh: 」希亮曰：「不知，與吾父同任事者宜知之。

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "I do not know; those who served with my father ought to know."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang replied, "I do not know. Those who served with my father should know."

sentences.zh: 」渾都海怒，詬曰：「我焉得知之，其父今亡命東見皇帝矣！

translations.literal: Hunduhai in anger cursed, saying, "How should I know? His father has now fled east to see the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Hunduhai burst out angrily, "How should I know? His father has already fled east to join the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 」希亮曰：「若然，則何謂不知！

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "If that is so, then what do you mean by not knowing!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang said, "If that is so, what do you mean by saying you do not know?"

sentences.zh: 」阿藍答兒熟視渾都海曰：「此言深有意焉。

translations.literal: Alandar stared intently at Hunduhai and said, "These words carry deep meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Alandar fixed his gaze on Hunduhai and said, "Those words carry a great deal of meaning."

sentences.zh: 」詰希亮甚急。

translations.literal: He pressed Xiliang very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Xiliang hard for an answer.

sentences.zh: 希亮曰：「使吾知之，亦從而去，安得獨留！

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "If I had known, I would have gone away with him too; how could I have been left behind alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang said, "If I had known, I would have gone with him. How could I have been left behind alone?"

sentences.zh: 」阿藍答兒以為實，免其監蒞。

translations.literal: Alandar took this as true and released him from guarded custody.
translations.idiomatic: Alandar believed him and lifted the guard placed over him.

sentences.zh: 既而阿藍答兒、渾都海為大兵所殺，其殘卒北走，眾推哈剌不花為帥。

translations.literal: Before long Alandar and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; their remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Harabuhua commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Alandar and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main force. The survivors fled north and chose Harabuhua as their commander.

sentences.zh: 希亮潛匿甘州北黑水東沙陀中。

translations.literal: Xiliang hid secretly in the Shatuo country east of the Black River north of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang went into hiding in the Shatuo lands east of the Black River, north of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 殿兵已過十餘里，有尋馬者適至，老婢漏言，眾奄至，驅至肅州。

translations.literal: The rearguard had already passed more than ten li when horse-seekers happened to arrive; an old maidservant let the secret slip, the crowd suddenly came upon them, and they were driven to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rearguard had already marched more than ten li on when scouts came looking for horses. An old servant let the secret slip, the troops descended on them at once, and they were driven to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花與鑄有婚姻之好，又哈剌不花在蜀時，嘗疾病，鑄召醫視之,遺以酒食， 因釋希亮縛，謂曰：「我受恩於汝父，此圖報之秋也。

translations.literal: Harabuhua and Zhu were joined by marriage ties; moreover, when Harabuhua was in Shu he had once fallen ill, and Zhu summoned a physician to attend him and sent wine and food; therefore he released Xiliang's bonds and said, "I received favor from your father—this is the season to repay it."
translations.idiomatic: Harabuhua was connected to Zhu by marriage, and when Harabuhua had fallen ill in Shu, Zhu had sent a physician and provided wine and food. He therefore released Xiliang from his bonds and said, "Your father once showed me kindness. Now is the time to repay it."

sentences.zh: 」及抵沙州北川，希亮與兄弟徒步負任，不火食者數日。

translations.literal: When they reached the northern stream of Shazhou, Xiliang and his brothers went on foot carrying burdens and went several days without cooked food.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the northern reaches of Shazhou, Xiliang and his brothers went on foot carrying their packs and went several days without a cooked meal.

sentences.zh: 是冬，涉雪逾天山，至北庭都護府。

translations.literal: That winter they crossed snow over the Tianshan range and reached the Protectorate General of Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they crossed the snow-covered Tianshan and reached the Protectorate General of Beiting.

sentences.zh: 二年，至昌八里城。

translations.literal: In the second year they reached Changbali City.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they reached Changbali.

sentences.zh: 夏，逾馬納思河，抵葉密里城，乃定宗潛邸湯沐之邑也。

translations.literal: In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili City, which was the bath-town appanage of Ögedei's princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they crossed the Manasi River and came to Yemili, the appanage town attached to Ögedei's princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 時六皇后之妹主後位，與宗王火忽皆欲東覲。

translations.literal: At that time the younger sister of Empress Dowager Töregene held the rear position, and she together with the imperial prince Huohu both wished to go east to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Töregene's younger sister held the empress's place, and she and the prince Huohu both wished to go east to pay homage at court.

sentences.zh: 希亮母密知其事，攜希亮入見，已而事不果。

translations.literal: Xiliang's mother secretly learned of the matter, took Xiliang in to see her, but in the end the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang's mother learned of the plan in secret and brought Xiliang in to see her, but in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 冬，至於火孛之地。

translations.literal: In winter they reached the land of Huobie.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they reached the land of Huobie.

sentences.zh: 三年，定宗幼子大名王閔其不能歸，遺以幣帛鞍馬，乃從大名王至忽只兒之地。

translations.literal: In the third year Ögedei's youngest son, Prince Daming, pitying that they could not return home, sent them silks, cloth, saddles, and horses; they then followed Prince Daming to Huzhier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ögedei's youngest son, Prince Daming, took pity on their inability to return home and gave them silks, cloth, saddles, and horses. They then followed the prince to Huzhier.

sentences.zh: 會宗王阿魯忽至，誅阿里不哥所用鎮守之人唆羅海，欲附世祖。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial prince Arigh Böke arrived, executed Suoluo Hai, whom Ariq Böke had placed in garrison, and wished to attach himself to Emperor Kublai.
translations.idiomatic: The prince Arigh Böke then arrived, executed Suoluo Hai, whom Ariq Böke had left as garrison commander, and sought to join Kublai.

sentences.zh: 復從大名王及阿魯忽二王還至葉密里城。

translations.literal: They again followed Princes Daming and Arigh Böke back to Yemili City.
translations.idiomatic: They then followed Princes Daming and Arigh Böke back to Yemili.

sentences.zh: 王遺以耳環，其二珠大如榛，實價直千金，欲穿其耳使帶之。

translations.literal: The prince gave him ear-rings; their two pearls were as large as hazelnuts and truly worth a thousand in gold; he wished to pierce his ears to make him wear them.
translations.idiomatic: The prince gave him a pair of earrings whose pearls were as large as hazelnuts and worth a thousand pieces of gold, and wanted to pierce his ears so that he could wear them.

sentences.zh: 希亮辭曰：「不敢因是以傷父母之遺體也。

translations.literal: Xiliang declined, saying, "I dare not for this reason injure the bodily form my parents bequeathed."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang declined, saying, "I dare not injure the body my parents gave me for such a reason."

sentences.zh: 且無功受賞，於禮尤不可。

translations.literal: Moreover, to receive reward without merit is especially impermissible in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, to accept a reward without having earned it is utterly contrary to propriety.

sentences.zh: 」王又解金束帶遺之，且曰：「系此，於遺體宜無傷。

translations.literal: The prince again removed a gold belt-girdle and gave it to him, saying, "Fasten this—it should not harm the bodily form bequeathed."
translations.idiomatic: The prince then took off a gold belt and gave it to him, saying, "Wear this instead—it should do no injury to the body your parents gave you."

sentences.zh: 」五月，又為阿里不哥兵所驅，西行千五百里，至孛劣撒里之地。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they were again driven by Ariq Böke's troops, traveling west fifteen hundred li to the place of Biliesali.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ariq Böke's troops drove them west again for fifteen hundred li to Biliesali.

sentences.zh: 六月，又西至換扎孫之地。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they again went west to the place of Huanzhasun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they marched farther west to Huanzhasun.

sentences.zh: 又從至不剌城。

translations.literal: They again followed on to Bula City.
translations.idiomatic: They continued on to Bula.

sentences.zh: 又西行六百里，至徹徹里澤剌之山，后妃輜重皆留於此，希亮母及兄弟亦在焉。

translations.literal: They again went west six hundred li to Mount Checheli Zelie; the empresses' and consorts' baggage trains were all left here, and Xiliang's mother and brothers were also there.
translations.idiomatic: They marched another six hundred li west to Mount Checheli Zelie, where the empresses' baggage was left behind along with Xiliang's mother and brothers.

sentences.zh: 希亮單騎從行二百餘里，至出布兒城。

translations.literal: Xiliang alone on horseback followed the march more than two hundred li to Chubuer City.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang rode alone with the column for more than two hundred li to Chubuer.

sentences.zh: 又百里，至也裡虔城，而哈剌不花之兵奄至，希亮又從二王興師，還至不剌城，與哈剌不花戰，敗之，盡殲其眾。

translations.literal: Another hundred li to Yeliqian City, and Harabuhua's troops suddenly arrived; Xiliang again followed the two princes in raising troops, returned to Bula City, fought Harabuhua, defeated him, and annihilated his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred li brought them to Yeliqian, where Harabuhua's army suddenly appeared. Xiliang again followed the two princes as they raised troops, marched back to Bula, defeated Harabuhua, and wiped out his force to the last man.

sentences.zh: 二王乃函其頭，遣使報捷。

translations.literal: The two princes then boxed his head and sent envoys to report the victory.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes placed his head in a box and sent messengers to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 十月，至於亦思寬之地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they reached the place of Yisikuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they reached Yisikuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，至可失哈里城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they reached Keshahari City.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they reached Keshahari.

sentences.zh: 四月，阿里不哥兵復至，希亮又從征，至渾八升城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Ariq Böke's troops came again; Xiliang again followed the campaign to Hunbasheng City.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ariq Böke's army returned, and Xiliang again joined the campaign as far as Hunbasheng.

sentences.zh: 時希亮母從後避暑於阿體八升山。

translations.literal: At that time Xiliang's mother followed in the rear to escape the heat at Mount Atibasheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiliang's mother had gone to the rear to escape the summer heat at Mount Atibasheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，鑄嘗言於世祖：「臣之妻子皆在北邊。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu had once said to Emperor Kublai, "Your servant's wife and children are all in the northern borderlands."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu had told Kublai, "Your servant's wife and children are all still in the north."

sentences.zh: 」至是，世祖遣不華出至二王所，因以璽書召希亮，馳驛赴闕。

translations.literal: At this point Emperor Kublai sent Buhua out to the two princes' place and, by imperial sealed letter, summoned Xiliang, who sped by post-stages to court.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor sent Buhua to the two princes with a sealed summons for Xiliang, who raced by relay to court.

sentences.zh: 六月，由苦先城至哈剌火州，出伊州，涉大漠以還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he went from Kuxian City to Karahuozhou, left by Yizhou, crossed the great desert, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he went from Kuxian to Karahuozhou, left by way of Yizhou, crossed the great desert, and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 八月，入覲世祖於上都之大安閣，備陳邊事，及羈旅困苦之狀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he entered audience with Emperor Kublai at the Great Peace Pavilion in Shangdu, fully setting forth border affairs and the hardships of his long exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he had audience with Kublai in the Great Peace Pavilion at Shangdu and gave a full account of frontier affairs and the hardships of his years abroad.

sentences.zh: 世祖憐之，賜鈔千錠、金帶一、幣帛三十，命為速古兒赤、必阇赤。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him, bestowed a thousand ingots of paper money, one gold belt, and thirty pieces of silks and cloth, and appointed him sughurji and bitichi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him, gave him a thousand ingots of paper money, a gold belt, and thirty pieces of silk and cloth, and appointed him attendant and scribe.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，授奉訓大夫、符寶郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Grand Master for Court Instruction and Keeper of the Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was made Grand Master for Court Instruction and Keeper of the Seals and Credentials.

sentences.zh: 十二年，既平宋，世祖命希亮問諸降將，日本可伐否。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, after the Song had been pacified, Emperor Kublai ordered Xiliang to ask the surrendered generals whether Japan could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after the conquest of the Song, Kublai ordered Xiliang to ask the surrendered generals whether Japan could be invaded.

sentences.zh: 夏貴、呂文煥、範文虎、陳奕等皆云可伐。

translations.literal: Xia Gui, Lü Wenhuan, Fan Wenhü, Chen Yi, and the others all said it could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui, Lü Wenhuan, Fan Wenhü, Chen Yi, and the others all said that it could.

sentences.zh: 希亮奏曰：「宋與遼、金攻戰且三百年，干戈甫定，人得息肩，俟數年，興師未晚。

translations.literal: Xiliang memorialized, saying, "The Song fought with Liao and Jin for nearly three hundred years; arms have only just been laid down and the people have barely rested their shoulders—wait several years and raising troops will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang memorialized, "The Song waged war against Liao and Jin for nearly three hundred years. Arms have only just been laid down and the people have barely had a moment's rest. Wait a few years before sending troops—it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」世祖然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，太府監令史盧贄言於監官：「各路所貢布長三丈，唯平陽加一丈，諸怯薛歹以故爭取平陽布。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Grand Provisionery clerk Lu Zan said to the supervising official, "The cloth presented from each circuit is three zhang in length, but Pingyang alone adds one zhang; the various keshik for this reason struggle to obtain Pingyang cloth."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Lu Zan, a clerk of the Grand Provisionery, told his supervisor, "Each circuit presents cloth three zhang long, but Pingyang alone adds an extra zhang, and for that reason the imperial guards all scramble for Pingyang cloth."

sentences.zh: 苟截其長者，與他郡等，則無所爭，而以其所截者為髹漆宮殿器皿之用，甚便。

translations.literal: If the extra length were cut off to make it equal to other prefectures, there would be no contention, and what was cut off could be used for lacquered palace vessels—very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: If the extra length were trimmed so that it matched the other prefectures, there would be no dispute, and the trimmed pieces could be used for lacquered palace vessels—a very practical arrangement.

sentences.zh: 」監官從之。

translations.literal: The supervising official followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor agreed.

sentences.zh: 適左右以其事聞，帝以詰監官，監官倉皇莫知所以對，歸罪於贄，帝命斬之。

translations.literal: It happened that attendants reported the matter; the emperor questioned the supervising official, who in panic did not know how to reply and shifted blame onto Zan; the emperor ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants happened to report the matter to the emperor, who questioned the supervisor. The man panicked and could not answer, blamed Zan, and the emperor ordered Zan executed.

sentences.zh: 希亮遇諸途，贄以冤告。

translations.literal: Xiliang met him on the road; Zan pleaded that he was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang met him on the road, and Zan pleaded that he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 希亮命少緩，具以實入奏。

translations.literal: Xiliang ordered a brief delay and fully reported the facts in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang told them to wait and submitted a full report of the facts.

sentences.zh: 有旨令董文用讞之。

translations.literal: There was an order that Dong Wenyong should judge the case.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Dong Wenyong to review the case.

sentences.zh: 竟釋贄，而召御史大夫塔察兒等讓之曰：「此事言官當言而不言，向微禿忽思，不誤誅此人耶！

translations.literal: In the end Zan was released, and the Censor-in-Chief Tachar and others were summoned and reproached, saying, "In this matter the remonstrance officials ought to have spoken but did not—had it not been for Tuhusi, would this man not have been wrongly executed!"
translations.idiomatic: Zan was released in the end, and the censor-in-chief Tachar and others were summoned and rebuked: "The remonstrance officials should have spoken up in this matter. Had it not been for Tuhusi, would we not have executed an innocent man by mistake?"

sentences.zh: 」十四年，轉嘉議大夫、禮部尚書，尋遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Grand Master of Court Discussion and Minister of Rites, and soon moved to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Court Discussion and Minister of Rites, and soon afterward transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝駐蹕察納兒台之地，希亮至，奏對畢，董文用問大都近事。

translations.literal: The emperor was encamped at Chanaiertai; when Xiliang arrived and finished his audience, Dong Wenyong asked about recent affairs in Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was encamped at Chanaiertai, Xiliang arrived and finished his audience. Dong Wenyong then asked him about recent affairs in Dadu.

sentences.zh: 希亮曰：「囹圄多囚耳。

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "The prisons simply have many prisoners—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang said, "The prisons are simply full—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」世祖方欹枕而臥，忽寤，問其故。

translations.literal: Emperor Kublai had been reclining on his pillow, but suddenly awoke and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had been dozing on his pillow, but he started awake and asked why.

sentences.zh: 希亮奏曰：「近奉旨：漢人盜鈔六文者殺。

translations.literal: Xiliang memorialized, saying, "Recently there was an order: Han people who steal six cash of paper money are to be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang replied, "A recent order says that any Han person who steals six cash of paper money is to be executed."

sentences.zh: 以是囚多。

translations.literal: For this reason there are many prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the prisons are so crowded.

sentences.zh: 」帝驚問：「孰傳此語？

translations.literal: The emperor in alarm asked, "Who transmitted these words?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked in alarm, "Who spread that saying?"

sentences.zh: 」省臣曰：「此旨實脫兒察所傳。

translations.literal: A provincial minister said, "This order was in fact transmitted by To'ercha."
translations.idiomatic: A minister of the Secretariat said, "It was To'ercha who passed it along."

sentences.zh: 」脫兒察曰：「陛下在南坡，以語蒙古兒童。

translations.literal: To'ercha said, "Your Majesty at Nanpo spoke it to Mongol children."
translations.idiomatic: To'ercha said, "Your Majesty said it in jest to some Mongol boys at Nanpo."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「前言戲耳，曷嘗著為令式？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What was said before was only in jest—when was it ever set down as a formal regulation?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That was only a joke. When did I ever turn it into law?"

sentences.zh: 」乃罪脫兒察。

translations.literal: He then punished To'ercha.
translations.idiomatic: He then punished To'ercha.

sentences.zh: 希亮因奏曰：「令既出矣，必明其錯誤，以安民心。

translations.literal: Xiliang thereupon memorialized, saying, "Since the order has already gone forth, its error must be made clear to reassure the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang then said, "Once an order has gone out, its mistake must be made plain so that the people may be reassured."

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言，即命希亮至大都，諭旨中書。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and at once ordered Xiliang to Dadu to proclaim the edict to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and immediately sent Xiliang to Dadu to announce the corrected edict to the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十七年，希亮以跋涉西土，足病痿攣，謝事而去，退居惣陽者二十餘年。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Xiliang, because of tramping through the western lands and foot ailment with withered paralysis, resigned office and left, retiring to Zongyang for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, worn out by years of travel in the west and crippled by paralysis of the legs, he resigned and withdrew to Zongyang, where he lived in retirement for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，武宗訪求先朝舊臣，特除翰林學士承旨、資善大夫，尋改授翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida Emperor Wuzong sought out old ministers of the former court and specially appointed him Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Grand Master of Excellent Virtue; soon he was reappointed Academician Expositor-in-Chief, Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida, Emperor Wuzong sought out veterans of the previous reign and specially appointed him Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Grand Master of Excellent Virtue. Soon afterward he was given the additional posts of drafter of imperial edicts and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 希亮以職在史官，乃類次世祖嘉言善行以進，英宗取其書，置禁中。

translations.literal: Xiliang, because his office lay among the historiographers, then arranged by category Emperor Kublai's fine words and good deeds and presented them; Emperor Yingzong took his book and placed it within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: As a historian, Xiliang compiled Kublai's memorable words and worthy deeds and presented the work to the throne. Emperor Yingzong took the book and kept it in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，閒居京師，四方之士多從之遊。

translations.literal: After a long while he lived at leisure in the capital, and scholars from the four quarters mostly associated with him in study.
translations.idiomatic: In time he settled in the capital, and scholars from all directions came to study with him.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taiding at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 希亮性至孝，困厄遐方，家貲散亡已盡，僅藏祖考畫像，四時就穹廬陳列致奠，盡誠盡敬。

translations.literal: Xiliang's nature was supremely filial; in hardship in distant regions the family wealth had scattered and perished entirely, and he kept only portraits of his ancestors and forebears, at the four seasons setting them out in the yurt to offer sacrifice with utmost sincerity and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang was profoundly filial. Though hardship in distant lands had stripped his family of everything, he kept only portraits of his ancestors and, at each season, set them out in his yurt to offer sacrifice with the utmost sincerity and respect.

sentences.zh: 朔漠之人，咸相聚來觀，歎曰：「此中土之禮也。

translations.literal: People of the northern deserts all gathered to come and watch, sighing, "This is the ritual of the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: People of the northern steppe gathered to watch and marveled, "This is the ritual of China proper."

sentences.zh: 」雖疾病，不廢書史，或中夜起坐，取燭以書。

translations.literal: Even when ill he did not abandon books and histories; sometimes in the middle of the night he would rise, take a candle, and write.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he was ill he never set aside his books. Sometimes he would rise in the middle of the night, light a candle, and write.

sentences.zh: 所著詩文及從軍紀行錄三十卷，目之曰《愫軒集》。

translations.literal: His compositions in poetry and prose together with records of campaigning in thirty juan he titled the 《Su Studio Collection》.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry, prose, and campaign diaries filled thirty juan, which he titled the 《Su Studio Collection》.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠輔義守正功臣、資善大夫、集賢學士、上護軍，追封漆水郡公，諡忠嘉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Righteousness, and Upholds Integrity, Grand Master of Excellent Virtue, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents, and Chief Commander of the Upper Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui Commandery; posthumous name Zhongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Righteousness, and Upholds Integrity, with the ranks of Grand Master of Excellent Virtue, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents, and Chief Commander of the Upper Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui, and given the posthumous name Zhongjia.

sentences.zh: 趙世延

translations.literal: Zhao Shiyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan

sentences.zh: 趙世延，字子敬，其先雍古族人，居雲中北邊。

translations.literal: Zhao Shiyan, courtesy name Zijing, his ancestors were Yonggu people dwelling on the northern border of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from the Yonggu people, who lived on the northern border of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖公，為金群牧使，太祖得其所牧馬，公死之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather the Duke served as Jin Director of Herds; when Taizu obtained the horses he pastured, the duke died for it.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather, known as the Duke, was director of herds under the Jin. When Genghis Khan seized the horses under his charge, the Duke died defending them.

sentences.zh: 祖按竺邇，幼孤，鞠於外大父術要甲，訛為趙家，因氏為趙；

translations.literal: His grandfather Anzhuer was orphaned young, reared by his maternal grandfather Shuyao Jia, mistakenly called the Zhao family, and therefore took Zhao as surname;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Anzhuer was orphaned in childhood and raised by his maternal grandfather Shuyao Jia. The family was mistakenly taken for the Zhao clan, and so they adopted Zhao as their surname.

sentences.zh: 驍勇善騎射，從太祖征伐，有功，為蒙古漢軍徵行大元帥，鎮蜀，因家成都。

translations.literal: Bold and brave, skilled in riding and archery, he followed Taizu on campaigns and had merit, becoming Grand Marshal on Campaign of the Mongol Han Army, garrisoning Shu, and therefore making his home in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and skilled in horsemanship and archery, followed Genghis Khan on campaign with distinction, became Grand Marshal on Campaign of the Mongol Han Army, garrisoned Shu, and made his home in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 父黑梓，以門功襲父元帥職，兼文州吐蕃萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: His father Heizi, by hereditary merit of the family, inherited his father's marshal post and concurrently served as darughachi of the Wenzou Tubo Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heizi inherited the family marshal's post by hereditary merit and also served as darughachi of the Wenzou Tubo Ten-thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 世延天資秀發，喜讀書，究心儒者體用之學。

translations.literal: Shiyan by nature was brilliantly gifted, delighted in reading books, and devoted his mind to the Confucian learning of substance and function.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan was gifted and quick-minded, loved reading, and devoted himself to the Confucian study of principle and practical application.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，世祖召見，俾入樞密院御史臺肄習官政。

translations.literal: At weak-crown age, Emperor Kublai summoned him and had him enter the Bureau of Military Affairs and Censorate to study official administration.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, Emperor Kublai summoned him and had him train in government at the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年，授承事郎、雲南諸路提刑按察司判官，時年二十有四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan, he was appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs and Adjucator of the Yunnan Circuit Provincial Surveillance Commission; he was then twenty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the Zhiyuan era (1284), he was appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs and adjucator of the Yunnan Circuit Provincial Surveillance Commission, at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙蠻酋叛，世延會省臣以軍討之，蠻兵大潰，即請降。

translations.literal: The Wumeng tribal chieftain rebelled; Shiyan joined provincial officials with troops to suppress him; the barbarian army was greatly routed and immediately sought surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wumeng chieftain rebelled, Shiyan joined the provincial officials in a military campaign against him. The tribal forces were routed and at once sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢監察御史，與同列五人劾丞相桑哥不法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was promoted to Supervising Censor; with five colleagues he impeached Chancellor Sangge for illegal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, he was promoted to supervising censor. He and five colleagues jointly impeached Chancellor Sangge for unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 中丞趙國輔，桑哥黨也，抑不以聞，更以告桑哥。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Guofu was a member of Sangge's faction; he suppressed the report and did not pass it upward, and instead informed Sangge.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Guofu, a partisan of Sangge, suppressed the memorial and never reported it to the throne, but instead told Sangge.

sentences.zh: 於是五人者悉為其所擠，而世延獨倖免。

translations.literal: Thereupon all five men were driven out by him, but Shiyan alone narrowly escaped.
translations.idiomatic: All five of his colleagues were then forced out, but Shiyan alone narrowly escaped.

sentences.zh: 奉旨按平陽郡監也先忽都贓巨萬，鞫左司郎中董仲威殺人獄，皆明允。

translations.literal: By imperial order he investigated Ye Xianhudu, supervisor of Pingyang Commandery, whose bribes amounted to tens of thousands; he also tried the murder case of Left Department Director Dong Zhongwei—all were clearly and fairly decided.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he investigated Ye Xianhudu, the Pingyang commandery supervisor, whose bribes ran to tens of thousands of cash. He also tried the murder case of Dong Zhongwei, director of the Left Department—all were judged clearly and fairly.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，轉奉議大夫，出僉江南湖北道肅政廉訪司事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was transferred to Gentleman for Discussion and sent out as Deputy Commissioner of the Jiangnan-Hubei Circuit Commission for Rectifying Governance and Supervising Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, he was transferred to Gentleman for Discussion and dispatched as deputy commissioner of the Jiangnan-Hubei Circuit Commission for Rectifying Governance and Supervising Officials.

sentences.zh: 敦儒學，立義倉，撤淫祠，修澧陽縣壞堤，嚴常、澧掠賣良民之禁，部內晏然。

translations.literal: He promoted Confucian learning, established charity granaries, demolished licentious shrines, repaired the damaged dyke at Liyang County, strictly enforced the ban on abducting and selling commoners in Chang and Li, and within his jurisdiction all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged Confucian learning, established charity granaries, demolished illicit shrines, and repaired the broken dyke at Liyang County. He strictly enforced the prohibition on kidnapping and selling commoners in Chang and Li, and the region under his charge grew calm.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，除江南行御史臺都事，丁內艱，不赴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate; when his mother died he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen, he was appointed chief clerk of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, but when his mother died he did not take up the office.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，复除前官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, he was again appointed to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade, he was again appointed to his former post.

sentences.zh: 三年，移中臺都事，俄改中書左司都事。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Central Censorate; soon after he was changed to Chief Clerk of the Left Department of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to chief clerk of the Central Censorate, and soon after was reassigned as chief clerk of the Left Department of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臺臣奏，仍為都事中臺。

translations.literal: Censorate officials memorialized, and he remained Chief Clerk at the Central Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate officials memorialized the throne, and he remained chief clerk at the Central Censorate.

sentences.zh: 六年，由山東肅政廉訪副使改江南行臺治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, from Deputy Commissioner of the Shandong Commission for Rectifying Governance he was changed to Investigative Attendant Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was moved from deputy commissioner of the Shandong Commission for Rectifying Governance to investigative attendant censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十年，除安西路總管。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Prefect of Anxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed prefect of Anxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 安西，故京兆省臺所治，號稱會府，前政壅滯者三千牘。

translations.literal: Anxi was formerly administered by the Jingzhao provincial and censorial offices, known as a metropolitan prefecture; the previous administration had three thousand stalled documents.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi had formerly been governed by the Jingzhao provincial and censorial offices and was known as a metropolitan prefecture. The previous administration had left three thousand cases backlogged.

sentences.zh: 世延既至，不三月，剖決殆盡。

translations.literal: Once Shiyan arrived, within three months nearly all were decided.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shiyan took office, he cleared nearly all of them within three months.

sentences.zh: 陝民飢，省臺議請於朝賑之，世延曰：「救荒如救火，願先發廩以賑，朝廷設不允，世延當傾家財若身以償。

translations.literal: The people of Shaanxi were starving; the provincial and censorial offices discussed requesting relief from the court. Shiyan said, "Famine relief is like fighting fire—I wish first to open the granaries to provide relief. If the court does not approve, Shiyan will exhaust his family wealth and person to repay."
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Shaanxi were starving, the provincial and censorial offices debated asking the court for relief. Shiyan said, "Relieving famine is like fighting a fire. I ask permission to open the granaries at once. If the court refuses, I will repay the cost from my own family fortune and my own person."

sentences.zh: 」省臺從之，所活者眾。

translations.literal: The provincial and censorial offices agreed; many lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial and censorial offices agreed, and many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，除紹興路總管，改四川肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, he was appointed Prefect of Shaoxing Circuit, then changed to Commissioner of the Sichuan Commission for Rectifying Governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed prefect of Shaoxing Circuit, then transferred to commissioner of the Sichuan Commission for Rectifying Governance.

sentences.zh: 蒙古軍士，科差繁重，而軍士就戍往來者多害人，且軍官或抑良為奴，世延皆除其弊而正其罪。

translations.literal: Mongol soldiers bore heavy levies, and soldiers going to and from garrison duty often harmed people; moreover officers sometimes coerced commoners into slavery—Shiyan removed all such abuses and punished the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol soldiers were burdened with heavy levies, and troops traveling to and from garrison duty often preyed on the people. Some officers even forced commoners into slavery. Shiyan eliminated these abuses and punished the offenders.

sentences.zh: 又修都江堰，民尤便之。

translations.literal: He also repaired the Dujiangyan irrigation works, which especially benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also restored the Dujiangyan irrigation system, to the people's great benefit.

sentences.zh: 四年，升中奉大夫、陝西行臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Attendant Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to grand master of palace attendance and appointed attendant censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，八百媳婦為邊患，右丞劉深往討之，兵敗而還，坐罪棄市。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Babai Xifu had been a frontier menace; Right Chancellor Liu Shen went to suppress them, his army was defeated and he returned, and he was executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Babai Xifu people had troubled the frontier. Right Chancellor Liu Shen marched against them, but his army was defeated and he returned to face execution.

sentences.zh: 及是，右丞阿忽台當繼行，世延言：「蠻夷事在羈縻，而重煩天討，致軍旅亡失，誅戮省臣，藉使盡得其地，何補於國？

translations.literal: At this time Right Chancellor Ahutai was to succeed him on campaign. Shiyan said, "Barbarian affairs should be handled by loose reins; yet repeatedly troubling Heaven's punitive expedition leads to loss of armies and execution of provincial ministers—even if we fully gained their land, what would it benefit the state?"
translations.idiomatic: When Right Chancellor Ahutai was about to take over the campaign, Shiyan said, "Barbarian affairs are best managed through loose reins. Yet we repeatedly send imperial armies against them, losing troops and executing provincial ministers. Even if we conquered every inch of their territory, what good would it do the state?"

sentences.zh: 今窮兵黷武，實傷聖治。

translations.literal: Now exhausting the armies and indulging in warfare truly harms sagely governance.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust the armies in endless war truly wounds the sage's rule.

sentences.zh: 朝廷第當選重臣知治體者，付以邊寄，兵宜止勿用。

translations.literal: The court should simply select heavy ministers who understand governance, entrust them with frontier affairs, and the armies should stop and not be used.
translations.idiomatic: The court should choose senior ministers who understand governance, entrust the frontier to them, and halt the use of force.

sentences.zh: 」事聞，樞密院臣以為用兵國家大事，不宜以一人之言為興輟。

translations.literal: When this was reported, Bureau of Military Affairs officials held that employing armies is a great state matter and should not be started or halted on one man's words.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs argued that war is a grave affair of state and should not be launched or abandoned on the word of one man.

sentences.zh: 世延聞之，章再上，事卒罷。

translations.literal: Shiyan heard this and memorialized again; in the end the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan heard of this and submitted another memorial. In the end the campaign was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，拜江浙行省參知政事，尋召還，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing, he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat; soon recalled and appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangqing he was appointed vice administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat. He was soon recalled and made attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，省臣奏：「比奉詔漢人參政用儒者，趙世延其人也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, provincial ministers memorialized, "Recently by imperial decree Han Chinese vice administrators should be Confucian scholars—Zhao Shiyan is such a man."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou the provincial ministers memorialized, "By recent imperial decree, Han Chinese vice administrators should be men of Confucian learning. Zhao Shiyan is such a man."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「世延誠可用，然雍古氏非漢人，其署宜居右。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Shiyan is truly usable, yet the Yonggu are not Han Chinese; his appointment should be on the right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shiyan is indeed fit for office, but the Yonggu are not Han Chinese, so his appointment should be on the right."

sentences.zh: 」遂拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed vice administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居中書二十月，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: After twenty months in the Secretariat, he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty months in the Secretariat, he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 有旨省臣自平章以下，率送之官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered provincial ministers from junior chancellor down to escort him to his office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required every provincial minister from the junior chancellor down to escort him to his new office.

sentences.zh: 其禮前所無有，由是為權臣所忌，乃用皇太后旨，出世延為雲南行省右丞。

translations.literal: Such ceremony had never existed before; thereby he was envied by powerful ministers, and by the empress dowager's order Shiyan was sent out as Right Chancellor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: No such honor had ever been granted before. Powerful ministers resented him, and by the empress dowager's order Shiyan was sent out as right chancellor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝特命仍還御史臺為中丞。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience, the emperor specially ordered him to return to the Censorate as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor specially ordered him back to the Censorate as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，世延劾奏權臣太師、右丞相帖木迭兒罪惡十有三，詔奪其官職。

translations.literal: In the third year, Shiyan memorialized impeaching the powerful minister Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor Bayan with thirteen counts of wrongdoing; an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shiyan impeached the powerful minister Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor Bayan on thirteen counts of misconduct. An edict stripped Bayan of his offices.

sentences.zh: 尋升翰林學士承旨，兼御史中丞，世延固辭，乃解中丞。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief; Shiyan firmly declined and was relieved of the vice censor-in-chief post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to academician chancellor of the Hanlin Academy while retaining the post of vice censor-in-chief. Shiyan firmly declined the dual appointment and was relieved of the censorate post.

sentences.zh: 五年，進光祿大夫、昭文館學士，守大都留守，乞補外，拜四川行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, promoted to Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness and Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, Acting Metropolitan Magistrate of Dadu; he requested an outside appointment and was appointed Junior Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to grand master of brilliant happiness and academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and served as acting metropolitan magistrate of Dadu. He asked for a provincial appointment and was made junior chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世延議即重慶路立屯田，物色江津、巴縣閒田七百八十三頃，摘軍千二百人墾之，歲得粟萬一千七百石。

translations.literal: Shiyan proposed establishing military colonies at Chongqing Circuit, located seven hundred eighty-three qing of land between Jiangjin and Ba Counties, assigned twelve hundred soldiers to cultivate it, yielding eleven thousand seven hundred shi of grain annually.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan proposed establishing military colonies at Chongqing Circuit. He located seven hundred eighty-three qing of land between Jiangjin and Ba Counties, assigned twelve hundred soldiers to farm it, and each year harvested eleven thousand seven hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 明年，仁宗崩，帖木迭兒复居相位，銳意報復，屬其黨何志道，誘世延從弟胥益兒哈呼誣告世延罪，逮世延置對，至夔路，遇赦。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Renzong died; Bayan again held the chancellorship and was bent on revenge; he ordered his partisan He Zhidao to induce Shiyan's younger cousin Xu Yierhahu to falsely accuse Shiyan; Shiyan was arrested for interrogation; reaching Kuizhou Circuit, he encountered an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Renzong died. Bayan returned to power and set out to settle scores. He had his partisan He Zhidao induce Shiyan's cousin Xu Yierhahu to lodge a false accusation. Shiyan was arrested and brought for trial. On the road to Kuizhou Circuit he met with a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 世延以疾抵荊門，留就醫。

translations.literal: Shiyan, ill, reached Jingmen and stayed for medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, Shiyan reached Jingmen and remained there for treatment.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒遣使督追至京師，俾其黨煅煉使成獄。

translations.literal: Bayan sent envoys to hurry him to the capital and had his partisans forge evidence to complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan sent agents to hurry him to the capital and ordered his followers to fabricate a conviction.

sentences.zh: 會有旨，事經赦原，勿復問。

translations.literal: There happened to be an edict that matters covered by amnesty should not be reinvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had just been issued stating that cases covered by amnesty were not to be reopened.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒更以它事白帝，系之刑曹，逼令自裁，世延不為動，居囚再歲。

translations.literal: Bayan reported other matters to the emperor, had him imprisoned in the penal office, pressured him to take his own life—Shiyan was unmoved and spent two years in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan raised new charges before the emperor, had Shiyan imprisoned in the penal office, and pressed him to kill himself. Shiyan did not waver and remained in custody for two years.

sentences.zh: 胥益兒哈呼自以所訴涉誣欺，亡去。

translations.literal: Xu Yierhahu himself, knowing his accusation involved falsehood, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yierhahu, realizing his accusation was fraudulent, fled.

sentences.zh: 中書左丞相拜住屢言世延亡辜，得旨出獄，就舍以養疾。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor of the Secretariat Baizhu repeatedly said Shiyan was innocent; he received an edict to leave prison and convalesce at home.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Baizhu repeatedly declared Shiyan innocent. An edict released him from prison, and he recuperated at home.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝獵北涼亭，顧謂侍臣曰：「趙世延先帝所尊禮，而帖木迭兒妄入其罪，數請誅之，此殆報私怨耳，朕豈能從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor hunted at Beiliang Pavilion and turned to tell attending ministers, "Zhao Shiyan was honored by the previous emperor, yet Bayan recklessly charged him with crimes and repeatedly asked to execute him—this is likely private revenge; how could I follow it?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while hunting at Beiliang Pavilion, the emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Zhao Shiyan was honored by my predecessor, yet Bayan falsely charged him and repeatedly asked for his execution. That is plainly private revenge. How could I agree to it?"

sentences.zh: 」侍臣皆叩頭稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The attending ministers all kowtowed and cried "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: The attending ministers all kowtowed and shouted their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒在上京，聞世延出獄，索省牘視之，怒曰：「此左丞相罔上所為也。

translations.literal: Bayan was at Shangdu; hearing Shiyan had left prison, he demanded the Secretariat documents and viewed them, angrily saying, "This was done by the left chancellor deceiving the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was at Shangdu. When he heard Shiyan had been released, he demanded the Secretariat documents and, after reading them, said angrily, "The left chancellor has deceived the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」事聞，帝語之曰：「此朕意耳。

translations.literal: When this was reported, the emperor told him, "This was my intention."
translations.idiomatic: When the remark reached the emperor, he told Bayan, "That was my own decision."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，帖木迭兒死，事乃釋。

translations.literal: Before long Bayan died and the matter was finally closed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bayan died, and the affair was finally laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 世延出居於金陵。

translations.literal: Shiyan went out and lived in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan withdrew and made his home in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，召還朝，除集賢大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, recalled to court, appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding he was recalled to court and appointed grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為江南行臺御史中丞。

translations.literal: The next year, sent out as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 四年，入朝，復為御史中丞，又遷中書右丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he entered court, again became Vice Censor-in-Chief, and was further transferred to Right Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court, again became vice censor-in-chief, and was then promoted to right vice chancellor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，有旨：趙世延頃為權奸所誣，中書宜遍移天下，昭雪其非辜，仍加翰林學士承旨、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict stated: Zhao Shiyan was lately slandered by powerful traitors; the Secretariat should send notices throughout the empire clearing his innocence, and he was further given Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict declared that Zhao Shiyan had been slandered by powerful traitors. The Secretariat was to circulate notices throughout the empire clearing his name, and he was further granted the titles of academician chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and grand master of brilliant happiness.

sentences.zh: 經筵開，兼知經筵事，選揀勸講者，皆一時名流。

translations.literal: When the Lectern was opened, he concurrently directed Lectern affairs; those selected as lecturers were all eminent men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial lectern was opened, he was put in charge of its affairs. The lecturers he chose were all leading figures of the day.

sentences.zh: 又加同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 泰定帝崩，燕鐵木兒與宗王大臣議：武宗二子周王、懷王，於法當立；

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiding died, Yan Temur with imperial princes and great ministers deliberated: Emperor Wuzong's two sons, the Prince of Zhou and the Prince of Huai, by law should be enthroned;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiding died, Yan Temur consulted with the imperial princes and senior ministers. By right, one of Emperor Wuzong's two sons—the Prince of Zhou and the Prince of Huai—should succeed;

sentences.zh: 周王遠在朔漠，而懷王久居民間，備嘗艱險，民必歸之，天位不可久虛，不如先迎懷王，以從民望。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhou was far in the northern desert, while the Prince of Huai had long lived among the people and experienced hardship—the people would surely rally to him; the throne cannot long be vacant—better first welcome the Prince of Huai to accord with the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: but the Prince of Zhou was far away in the northern steppe, whereas the Prince of Huai had long lived among the people and borne hardship. The people would surely rally to him. The throne could not remain empty, so it was better to welcome the Prince of Huai first and satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 八月，即定策，迎之於江陵，懷王即位，是為文宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they immediately settled the plan, welcomed him at Jiangling; the Prince of Huai ascended and this was Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they settled on this course, welcomed him at Jiangling, and the Prince of Huai ascended the throne as Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 當是時，世延贊畫之功為多。

translations.literal: At that time Shiyan's merit in planning and counsel was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shiyan's contribution to the planning was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，世延仍以御史中丞兼翰林學士承旨，以疾乞歸田里，詔不允。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended, Shiyan remained Vice Censor-in-Chief concurrently Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy; ill, he requested to return to his fields—the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, Shiyan remained vice censor-in-chief while also serving as academician chancellor of the Hanlin Academy. He pleaded illness and asked to retire to his home, but the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 天曆二年正月，复除江南行臺御史中丞；

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tianli, again appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Tianli he was again appointed vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate;

sentences.zh: 行次濟州，三月，改集賢大學士；

translations.literal: Stopping at Jizhou en route, in the third month changed to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents;
translations.idiomatic: while traveling he stopped at Jizhou, and in the third month was transferred to grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents;

sentences.zh: 六月，又加奎章閣大學士；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, further given Grand Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month he was further made grand academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 八月，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, appointed Junior Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and in the eighth month he was appointed junior chancellor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，世延至京，固辭不允，詔以世延年高多疾，許乘小車入內。

translations.literal: In winter Shiyan reached the capital, firmly declined but was not permitted; an edict, since Shiyan was elderly and often ill, allowed him to enter the palace in a small carriage.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Shiyan reached the capital. He tried again to decline the appointment, but was not permitted. An edict, noting his advanced age and frequent illness, allowed him to enter the palace in a small carriage.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，詔世延與虞集等纂修《皇朝經世大典》，世延屢奏：「臣衰老，乞解中書政務，專意纂修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun, an edict ordered Shiyan with Yu Ji and others to compile the "Records of Governance and Institutions"; Shiyan repeatedly memorialized, "Your subject is aged and feeble; I beg to be relieved of Secretariat duties to devote myself to compilation."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun an edict ordered Shiyan, together with Yu Ji and others, to compile the "Records of Governance and Institutions." Shiyan repeatedly memorialized, "I am old and infirm. I beg to be relieved of Secretariat duties so that I may devote myself entirely to the compilation."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「老臣如卿者無幾，求退之言，後勿復陳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Old ministers like you are few; speak no more of retirement hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "There are few old ministers like you. Do not speak of retirement again."

sentences.zh: 」四月，仍加翰林學士承旨，封魯國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he was still given Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was again granted the title of academician chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 秋，以疾，移文中書致其事，明日即行，養疾於金陵之茅山。

translations.literal: In autumn, owing to illness, he sent a letter to the Secretariat resigning his post; the next day he departed and convalesced at Mount Mao in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, citing illness, he sent a letter to the Secretariat resigning his office. The next day he set out and went to convalesce on Mount Mao near Jinling.

sentences.zh: 詔徵還朝，不能行，二年，改封涼國公。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him back to court; he could not travel; in the second year his title was changed to Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him back to court, but he was unable to travel. In the second year his title was changed to Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，詔賜世延錢凡四萬緡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong, an edict granted Shiyan forty thousand strings of cash in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuantong an edict granted Shiyan a total of forty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 至元改元，仍除奎章閣大學士、翰林學士承旨、中書平章政事、魯國公。

translations.literal: At the change of era name to Zhiyuan, he was again appointed Grand Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion, Academician Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, Junior Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When the era name was changed to Zhiyuan, he was again appointed grand academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion, academician chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, junior chancellor of the Secretariat, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，至成都，十一月卒，享年七十有七。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month he reached Chengdu; in the eleventh month he died, age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the fifth month, he reached Chengdu. In the eleventh month he died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，贈世忠執法佐運翊亮功臣、太保、金紫光祿大夫、上柱國，追封魯國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng, posthumously given Meritous Subject Who Served the Age with Loyalty, Upheld the Law, Assisted the Destiny, and Illumined the Court, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Robe, Pillar of the State of the Upper Rank; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Lu; posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizheng he was posthumously honored as Meritous Subject Who Served the Age with Loyalty, Upheld the Law, Assisted the Destiny, and Illumined the Court, with the ranks of grand preceptor, grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple robe, and pillar of the state of the upper rank. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 世延歷事凡九朝，揚歷省臺五十餘年，負經濟之資，而將之以忠義，守之以清介，飾之以文學，凡軍國利病，生民休戚，知無不言，而於儒者名教尤拳拳焉。

translations.literal: Shiyan served through nine reigns, rising through provincial and censorial offices for more than fifty years. He possessed the talent for statecraft, tempered it with loyalty and righteousness, guarded it with integrity, and adorned it with literary learning. In all matters of military and state advantage or harm, and the people's weal and woe, he spoke without reserve; and toward Confucian moral teaching he was especially earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan served nine reigns and spent more than fifty years in provincial and censorial office. He had the capacity for statecraft, yet tempered it with loyalty and righteousness, guarded it with integrity, and adorned it with learning. On every matter affecting army and state, and the people's welfare, he spoke without holding back; and he was especially devoted to Confucian moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 為文章波瀾浩瀚，一根於理。

translations.literal: His writings were vast and sweeping, rooted entirely in principle.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was broad and powerful, yet always rooted in principle.

sentences.zh: 嘗較定律令，匯次《風憲宏綱》，行於世。

translations.literal: He once compared and arranged statutes, compiled the "Comprehensive Statutes of Censorial Administration," which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He once collated the statutes and compiled the "Comprehensive Statutes of Censorial Administration," which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 五子，達者三人：野峻台，黃州路總管。

translations.literal: Five sons, three distinguished: Yejuntai, Prefect of Huangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons, of whom three rose to distinction: Yejuntai, prefect of Huangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 次月魯，江浙行省理問官。

translations.literal: Second, Yuelu, Inquiry Official of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The second, Yuelu, served as inquiry official of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 伯忽，夔州路總管，天曆初，囊加台據蜀叛，死於難，特贈推忠秉義效節功臣、資善大夫、中書右丞、上護軍，追封蜀郡公，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: Behu, Prefect of Kuizhou Circuit; at the beginning of Tianli, Nanggal Tai seized Shu in rebellion and Behu died in the turmoil; specially posthumously given Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Died in Service, Grand Master of Excellent Virtue, Right Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat, Chief Commander of the Upper Army; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Shu Commandery; posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Behu, prefect of Kuizhou Circuit. At the beginning of Tianli, when Nanggal Tai rebelled and seized Shu, Behu died in the upheaval. He was specially posthumously honored as Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Died in Service, with the ranks of grand master of excellent virtue, right vice chancellor of the Secretariat, and chief commander of the upper army. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shu and given the posthumous name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 孔思晦

translations.literal: Kong Sihui
translations.idiomatic: Kong Sihui

sentences.zh: 孔思晦，字明道，孔子五十四世孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Sihui, courtesy name Mingdao, was the fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Sihui, whose courtesy name was Mingdao, was a fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 資質端重，而性簡默，童丱時，讀書已識大義。

translations.literal: His nature was dignified and grave, yet reserved and silent; even as a child in his hair-knot years, in reading he already grasped great principles.
translations.idiomatic: He was dignified and reserved by nature. Even as a child he read with understanding and grasped the larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 及長，授業於導江張䇓，講求義理，於詞章之習，薄而弗為。

translations.literal: When grown, he received instruction from Zhang Yi of Daojiang, pursued moral principle, and held literary composition in slight regard, refusing to practice it.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied under Zhang Yi of Daojiang, devoting himself to moral principle while giving little attention to literary composition.

sentences.zh: 家貧，躬耕以為養，雖劇寒暑，而為學未嘗懈，遠近爭聘為子弟師。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he personally farmed to support them. Though heat and cold were severe, he never slackened in study, and people near and far competed to hire him as teacher for their sons.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he farmed with his own hands to support them. Through the harshest seasons he never slackened in his studies, and families near and far sought him out as a teacher for their sons.

sentences.zh: 大德中，遊京師，祭酒耶律有尚欲薦之，以母老，辭而歸。

translations.literal: In the Dade era he traveled to the capital; Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Yelü Youshang wished to recommend him, but because his mother was old he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era he went to the capital. Yelü Youshang, chancellor of the Directorate of Education, wished to recommend him, but he declined because his mother was elderly and returned home.

sentences.zh: 母臥疾，躬進藥餌，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: When his mother lay ill, he personally administered medicine and food and did not unfasten his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he personally tended her with medicine and food and never left her side.

sentences.zh: 居喪，勺水不入口者五日。

translations.literal: In mourning, for five days he did not take a spoonful of water into his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he went five days without taking even a spoonful of water.

sentences.zh: 至大中，舉茂才，為范陽儒學教諭。

translations.literal: In the Zhida era he was recommended as a maocai and appointed instructor at the Fanyang Confucian school.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhida era he was recommended as a maocai and appointed instructor at the Fanyang Confucian school.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，調寧陽學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou he was transferred to the Ningyang school.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yanyou he was transferred to the Ningyang school.

sentences.zh: 先是，兩縣校官率以廩薄不能守職，而思晦以儉約自將，教養有法，比代去，學者皆不忍舍之。

translations.literal: Earlier, school officials in both counties generally could not hold their posts because stipends were thin, but Sihui governed himself with frugality, had effective methods of teaching and nurturing, and when his term ended the students all were unwilling to part with him.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, school officials in both counties had usually been unable to remain in office because their stipends were too small. Sihui lived frugally, taught with method, and when his term ended his students were loath to see him go.

sentences.zh: 於是孔氏族人相與議：思晦嫡長且賢，宜襲封爵，奉祠事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Kong clansmen deliberated together: Sihui was the eldest legitimate son and worthy; he should inherit the enfeoffment and perform the sacrificial duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Kong clansmen then agreed among themselves that Sihui, as the eldest legitimate son and a man of virtue, ought to inherit the enfeoffment and preside over the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 狀上政府，事未決。

translations.literal: A petition was submitted to the government; the matter was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted a petition to the authorities, but the matter had not yet been settled.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在位，雅崇尚儒道，一日，問：「孔子之裔今幾世，襲爵為誰？

translations.literal: While Emperor Renzong reigned, he greatly honored Confucian teaching. One day he asked, "How many generations now are Confucius's descendants, and who holds the enfeoffment?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong greatly honored Confucian learning. One day he asked, "Which generation of Confucius's descendants are we in now, and who holds the hereditary title?"

sentences.zh: 」廷臣具對曰：「未定。

translations.literal: Court ministers answered in detail, "Not yet decided."
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers replied in full, "It has not yet been decided."

sentences.zh: 」帝親取孔氏譜牒按之，曰：「以嫡應襲封者，思晦也，复奚疑！

translations.literal: The emperor personally took the Kong clan genealogical registers and examined them, saying, "The one who by legitimate descent should inherit the enfeoffment is Sihui—what further doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally examined the Kong clan genealogies and said, "The legitimate heir to the title is Sihui. What room for doubt remains?"

sentences.zh: 」特授中議大夫，襲封衍聖公，月俸百緡，加至五百緡，賜四品印。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel, inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fulfilling the Sage, with a monthly salary of a hundred strings of cash increased to five hundred, and was granted a seal of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel and inherited the title Duke of Fulfilling the Sage, with a monthly stipend raised from one hundred to five hundred strings of cash and a seal of the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，山東廉訪副使王鵬南言：「襲爵上公，而階止四品，於格弗稱，且失尊崇意。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiding, Wang Pengnan, deputy commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission, said, "One who inherits a noble rank of the highest duke yet holds only fourth-rank status does not match the regulations and moreover fails the intent of honor."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiding, Wang Pengnan, deputy surveillance commissioner of Shandong, said, "The hereditary holder of a supreme ducal title should not remain at only the fourth rank. That falls short of the regulations and of the respect due the sage's line."

sentences.zh: 」明年，升嘉議大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Grand Master of Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Grand Master of Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，改賜三品印。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he was re-granted a seal of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun he was given a seal of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 思晦以宗祀責重，恆懼弗勝，每遇祭祀，必敬必慎。

translations.literal: Sihui, because the responsibility for ancestral sacrifice was weighty, constantly feared he might not measure up; whenever sacrifice came due, he was invariably reverent and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Because the duty of ancestral sacrifice weighed heavily upon him, Sihui constantly feared he might fall short. Whenever rites were performed, he was scrupulously reverent and careful.

sentences.zh: 初，廟毀於兵，後雖苟完，而角樓圍牆未備，思晦竭力營度，以復其舊。

translations.literal: At first the temple had been destroyed in warfare; later, though roughly restored, the corner towers and enclosing walls were not complete. Sihui labored with all his strength in planning and restored it to its former state.
translations.idiomatic: The temple had first been destroyed in war. Though it was later patched together, the corner towers and walls were still incomplete. Sihui threw himself into the work and restored it to its former condition.

sentences.zh: 金絲堂壞，又一新之，祭器禮服，悉加整飭。

translations.literal: The Hall of Gold Threads had fallen into ruin; he rebuilt it anew, and sacrificial vessels and ritual garments were all put in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Gold Threads had fallen into ruin, and he rebuilt it entirely. Sacrificial vessels and ritual garments were all put in proper order.

sentences.zh: 又以尼山乃毓聖之地，故有廟，已毀，民冒耕祭田且百年，思晦復其田，且請置尼山書院，以列於學官，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Mount Ni was the place where the sage was nurtured, there had been a temple there, but it was destroyed and the people had encroached to farm the sacrificial fields for nearly a century. Sihui recovered the fields and also requested establishment of the Mount Ni Academy to be listed among the official schools; the court assented.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Ni was where the sage had been nurtured, and though a temple once stood there, it had been destroyed and local people had farmed the sacrificial lands for nearly a century. Sihui recovered those fields and petitioned to establish the Mount Ni Academy as an official school, which the court approved.

sentences.zh: 三氏學舊有田三千畝，佔於豪民，子思書院舊有營運錢萬緡，貸於民取子錢，以供祭祀，久之，民不輸子錢，並負其本，思晦皆理而復之。

translations.literal: The Three Clans School formerly had three thousand mu of fields occupied by powerful families; the Zisi Academy formerly had ten thousand strings of operating funds lent to the people at interest to supply sacrifices. After a long time the people paid neither interest nor principal. Sihui settled all these matters and recovered them.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Clans School once held three thousand mu of land seized by powerful families, and the Zisi Academy had ten thousand strings of operating funds lent out at interest to finance sacrifices. In time the borrowers paid neither interest nor principal. Sihui investigated every case and recovered the assets.

sentences.zh: 聖父舊封齊國公，思晦言於朝曰：「宣聖封王，而父爵猶公，願加褒崇。

translations.literal: The sage's father had formerly been enfeoffed as Duke of Qi. Sihui said to the court, "The Exalted Sage was enfeoffed as king, yet his father's title remains duke. I ask that honor be increased."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's father had long held the title Duke of Qi. Sihui said to the court, "The Exalted Sage has been enfeoffed as king, yet his father's rank remains that of duke. I ask that greater honor be granted."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔加封聖父啟聖王，聖母王夫人。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict added the enfeoffment of the sage's father as King of Initiating the Sage and the sage's mother as Lady of the Royal House.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then raised Confucius's father to King of Initiating the Sage and his mother to Lady of the Royal House.

sentences.zh: 五季時，孔末之後方盛，欲以偽滅真，害宣聖子孫幾盡，至是，其裔复欲冒稱宣聖後。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period the descendants of Kong Mo had been flourishing and wished to destroy the true line with a false one, nearly exterminating the descendants of the Exalted Sage. At this time their offspring again wished falsely to claim descent from the Exalted Sage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties the descendants of Kong Mo had grown powerful and sought to supplant the true line, nearly wiping out Confucius's heirs. Now their descendants again tried to pass themselves off as heirs of the sage.

sentences.zh: 思晦以為：「不早辨則真偽久益不可明，彼與我不共戴天，乃列於族，與共拜殿庭，可乎？

translations.literal: Sihui considered, "If not distinguished early, true and false will long grow ever harder to clarify. They and I do not share the same sky—yet they are to be listed in the clan and worship together in the hall. How can that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Sihui said, "If we do not settle this early, truth and falsehood will only grow harder to tell apart. They are sworn enemies of our line. How can they be entered in the clan roll and worship with us in the temple hall?"

sentences.zh: 」遂會族人，稽典故斥之，既又重刻宗譜於石，而孔氏族裔益明矣。

translations.literal: He thereupon assembled the clansmen, examined classical precedents to reject them, and afterward re-cut the clan genealogy in stone, so that the Kong clan descent became still clearer.
translations.idiomatic: He then assembled the clan, cited precedent to reject them, and had the genealogy carved anew in stone, so that the Kong lineage became still clearer.

sentences.zh: 元統元年卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yuantong at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，有鶴百餘翔其屋上，又見神光自東南落其舍北。

translations.literal: On the day of his death more than a hundred cranes circled above his house, and a divine light was seen falling from the southeast onto the north side of his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, more than a hundred cranes circled above his house, and a divine light was seen descending from the southeast to the north side of his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 至正中，朝廷加贈其官，而賜諡曰文肅。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era the court added posthumous offices and granted the posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era the court added posthumous honors and gave him the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子曰克堅，襲封衍聖公，階嘉議大夫，既而進通奉大夫。

translations.literal: His son was Kejian, who inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fulfilling the Sage at the rank of Grand Master of Court Discussion and was later advanced to Grand Master for Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kejian inherited the title Duke of Fulfilling the Sage at the rank of Grand Master of Court Discussion and was later promoted to Grand Master for Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，召為同知太常禮儀院事，拜陝西行臺侍御史，遷國子祭酒，擢山東肅政廉訪使，不赴。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng he was summoned as associate administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed attendant censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, transferred to chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong, but he did not take up the last post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng he was summoned as deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, made attendant censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, transferred to chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong, but he declined the final appointment.

sentences.zh: 孫希學，襲封衍聖公。

translations.literal: His grandson Xixue inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fulfilling the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xixue inherited the title Duke of Fulfilling the Sage.
